celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿وَأَوْفُوا الْكَيْلَ﴾ complete it ﴿إِذَا كِلْتُمْ وَزِنُوا بِالْقِسْطَاسِ الْمُسْتَقِيمِ﴾ the true balance ﴿ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَحْسَنُ تَأْوِيلًا﴾ in outcome.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿وَلَا تَقْفُ﴾ do not follow ﴿مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤَادَ﴾ the heart ﴿كُلُّ أُولَئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا﴾ its owner [will be asked] what he did with it.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿وَلَا تَمْشِ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَحًا﴾ i.e. in a state of exultation, with pride and conceit ﴿إِنَّكَ لَنْ تَخْرِقَ الْأَرْضَ﴾ pierce it until you reach its far end by your pride ﴿وَلَنْ تَبْلُغَ الْجِبَالَ طُولًا﴾ The meaning is: you do not attain this extent, so how can you swagger?

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿كُلُّ ذَلِكَ﴾ that has been mentioned ﴿كَانَ سَيِّئُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ مَكْرُوهًا﴾

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ مِمَّا أَوْحَى إِلَيْكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿رَبُّكَ مِنَ الْحِكْمَةِ﴾ the admonition ﴿وَلَا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ فَتُلْقَى فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَلُومًا مَدْحُورًا﴾ driven away from the mercy of Allah.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿أَفَأَصْفَاكُمْ﴾ has He singled you out, O people of Mecca, ﴿رَبُّكُمْ بِالْبَنِينَ وَاتَّخَذَ مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ إِنَاثًا﴾ daughters for Himself, as you claim? ﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَتَقُولُونَ﴾ by that ﴿قَوْلًا عَظِيمًا﴾

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَا﴾ We have set forth clearly ﴿فِي هَذَا الْقُرْآنِ﴾ similitudes, promises and threats ﴿لِيَذَّكَّرُوا﴾ that they may take admonition ﴿وَمَا يَزِيدُهُمْ﴾ that ﴿إِلَّا نُفُورًا﴾ from the truth.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿لَوْ كَانَ مَعَهُ﴾ i.e. Allah ﴿آلِهَةٌ كَمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذًا لَابْتَغَوْا﴾ they would have sought ﴿إِلَى ذِي الْعَرْشِ﴾ i.e. Allah ﴿سَبِيلًا﴾ to fight Him.

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿سُبْحَانَهُ﴾ a declaration of His transcendence ﴿وَتَعَالَى عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ﴾ of partners ﴿عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا﴾

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ﴾ declare His transcendence ﴿السَّمَاوَاتُ السَّبْعُ وَالْأَرْضُ وَمَنْ فِيهِنَّ وَإِنْ﴾ not (إِنْ = مَا) ﴿مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾ of the created things ﴿إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ﴾ while joined ﴿بِحَمْدِهِ﴾ i.e. it says: "Glory be to Allah and with His praise" ﴿وَلَكِنْ لَا تَفْقَهُونَ﴾ you do not understand ﴿تَسْبِيحَهُمْ﴾ because it is not in your language ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورًا﴾ in that He did not hasten the punishment upon you.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿وَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ الْقُرْآنَ جَعَلْنَا بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ حِجَابًا مَسْتُورًا﴾ i.e. concealing you from them, so they do not see you. It was revealed concerning those who wanted to assassinate him ﷺ.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً﴾ coverings ﴿أَنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ﴾ [preventing them] from understanding the Quran, i.e. so they do not understand it ﴿وَفِي آذَانِهِمْ وَقْرًا﴾ heaviness, so they do not hear it ﴿وَإِذَا ذَكَرْتَ رَبَّكَ فِي الْقُرْآنِ وَحْدَهُ وَلَّوْا عَلَى أَدْبَارِهِمْ نُفُورًا﴾ from it.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَسْتَمِعُونَ بِهِ﴾ on account of which, namely mockery ﴿إِذْ يَسْتَمِعُونَ إِلَيْكَ﴾ to your recitation ﴿وَإِذْ هُمْ نَجْوَى﴾ they converse secretly among themselves, i.e. they talk ﴿إِذْ﴾ a badal (substitute) for the إِذْ before it ﴿يَقُولُ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ in their secret talk ﴿إِنْ﴾ not (إِنْ = مَا) ﴿تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا رَجُلًا مَسْحُورًا﴾ deceived, overcome in his mind. Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿انْظُرْ كَيْفَ ضَرَبُوا لَكَ الْأَمْثَالَ﴾ [likening you] to one bewitched, a soothsayer and a poet ﴿فَضَلُّوا﴾ thereby from guidance ﴿فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَبِيلًا﴾ a way to it.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ denying the resurrection ﴿أَإِذَا كُنَّا عِظَامًا وَرُفَاتًا أَإِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ خَلْقًا جَدِيدًا﴾

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿أَوْ خَلْقًا مِمَّا يَكْبُرُ فِي صُدُورِكُمْ﴾ which is too great [in your minds] to receive life, let alone bones and fragments; yet the spirit will certainly be brought into being in you ﴿فَسَيَقُولُونَ مَنْ يُعِيدُنَا﴾ to life? ﴿قُلِ الَّذِي فَطَرَكُمْ﴾ created you ﴿أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾ when you were nothing; for the One able to begin [creation] is able to repeat it; indeed, that is easier ﴿فَسَيُنْغِضُونَ﴾ they will shake ﴿إِلَيْكَ رُءُوسَهُمْ﴾ in astonishment ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ mockingly ﴿مَتَى هُوَ﴾ i.e. the resurrection ﴿قُلْ عَسَى أَنْ يَكُونَ قَرِيبًا﴾

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يَدْعُوكُمْ﴾ calls you from the graves by the tongue of Isrāfīl ﴿فَتَسْتَجِيبُونَ﴾ and you answer his call from the graves ﴿بِحَمْدِهِ﴾ by His command; and it is said: "and to Him belongs the praise" ﴿وَتَظُنُّونَ إِنْ﴾ not (إِنْ = مَا) ﴿لَبِثْتُمْ﴾ in the world ﴿إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾ because of the terror of what you see.

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿وَقُلْ لِعِبَادِي﴾ the believers ﴿يَقُولُوا﴾ to the disbelievers the word ﴿الَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يَنْزَغُ﴾ sows discord ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ كَانَ لِلْإِنْسَانِ عَدُوًّا مُبِينًا﴾ clear in enmity. And the word which is best is: [Translator's note: the sentence continues into the next entry, 17:54.]

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿رَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ إِنْ يَشَأْ يَرْحَمْكُمْ﴾ through repentance and faith ﴿أَوْ إِنْ يَشَأْ﴾ to punish you ﴿يُعَذِّبْكُمْ﴾ by death in disbelief ﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَكِيلًا﴾ so as to compel them to believe. This was before the command to fight.

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿وَرَبُّكَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ so He singles them out with what He wills according to their states ﴿وَلَقَدْ فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَ النَّبِيِّينَ عَلَى بَعْضٍ﴾ by distinguishing each of them with a merit: such as Moses with [direct] speech, Abraham with intimate friendship, and Muhammad with the Night Journey ﴿وَآتَيْنَا دَاوُدَ زَبُورًا﴾

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿ادْعُوا الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ﴾ that they are gods ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ such as the angels, Jesus and ʿUzayr ﴿فَلَا يَمْلِكُونَ كَشْفَ الضُّرِّ عَنْكُمْ وَلَا تَحْوِيلًا﴾ of it to others than you.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ﴾ them as gods ﴿يَبْتَغُونَ﴾ seek ﴿إِلَى رَبِّهِمُ الْوَسِيلَةَ﴾ nearness through obedience ﴿أَيُّهُمْ﴾ a badal (substitute) for the wāw of يَبْتَغُونَ, i.e. even the one who is ﴿أَقْرَبُ﴾ to Him seeks it, so how much more anyone else ﴿وَيَرْجُونَ رَحْمَتَهُ وَيَخَافُونَ عَذَابَهُ﴾ like others; so how can you call upon them as gods? ﴿إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّكَ كَانَ مَحْذُورًا﴾

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ not (إِنْ = مَا) ﴿مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ﴾ its people are meant ﴿إِلَّا نَحْنُ مُهْلِكُوهَا قَبْلَ يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾ by death ﴿أَوْ مُعَذِّبُوهَا عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا﴾ by killing and other means ﴿كَانَ ذَلِكَ فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Preserved Tablet ﴿مَسْطُورًا﴾ written.

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿وَمَا مَنَعَنَا أَنْ نُرْسِلَ بِالْآيَاتِ﴾ which the people of Mecca proposed ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ كَذَّبَ بِهَا الْأَوَّلُونَ﴾ when We sent them, so We destroyed them; and had We sent them to these [people], they [would have been destroyed too], whereas We have decreed to grant them respite in order to complete the mission of Muhammad ﷺ [Translator's note: the bracketed completion follows the evident sense; the Arabic leaves the apodosis of لَوْ unexpressed] ﴿وَآتَيْنَا ثَمُودَ النَّاقَةَ﴾ as a sign ﴿مُبْصِرَةً﴾ clear and evident ﴿فَظَلَمُوا﴾ they disbelieved ﴿بِهَا﴾ and so were destroyed ﴿وَمَا نُرْسِلُ بِالْآيَاتِ﴾ the miracles ﴿إِلَّا تَخْوِيفًا﴾ for the servants, so that they may believe.

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ قُلْنَا لَكَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ أَحَاطَ بِالنَّاسِ﴾ in knowledge and power, so they are in His grasp; so convey [the message] to them and fear no one, for He protects you from them ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا الرُّؤْيَا الَّتِي أَرَيْنَاكَ﴾ with your own eyes on the night of the Night Journey ﴿إِلَّا فِتْنَةً لِلنَّاسِ﴾ the people of Mecca, since they denied it and some of them apostatised when he told them of it ﴿وَالشَّجَرَةَ الْمَلْعُونَةَ فِي الْقُرْآنِ﴾ which is al-Zaqqūm, which grows at the bottom of Hellfire; We made it a trial for them, since they said: "Fire burns trees, so how can it make it grow?" ﴿وَنُخَوِّفُهُمْ﴾ with it ﴿فَمَا يَزِيدُهُمْ﴾ Our making them fear ﴿إِلَّا طُغْيَانًا كَبِيرًا﴾

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ﴾ a prostration of greeting, by bowing ﴿فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ قَالَ أَأَسْجُدُ لِمَنْ خَلَقْتَ طِينًا﴾ made accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. "from clay" (مِنْ طِينٍ).

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿قَالَ أَرَأَيْتَكَ﴾ i.e. tell me ﴿هَذَا الَّذِي كَرَّمْتَ﴾ You have preferred ﴿عَلَيَّ﴾ by commanding prostration to him, while I am better than him: You created me from fire ﴿لَئِنْ﴾ the lām of the oath ﴿أَخَّرْتَنِ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ لَأَحْتَنِكَنَّ﴾ I will surely uproot ﴿ذُرِّيَّتَهُ﴾ by leading them astray ﴿إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾ of them, those whom You have protected.

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ the Exalted to him: ﴿اذْهَبْ﴾ granted respite until the time of the first blast [of the Trumpet] ﴿فَمَنْ تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ فَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ جَزَاؤُكُمْ﴾ you and they ﴿جَزَاءً مَوْفُورًا﴾ ample and complete.

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿وَاسْتَفْزِزْ﴾ incite lightly ﴿مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ مِنْهُمْ بِصَوْتِكَ﴾ by your call, with singing, pipes and every caller to disobedience ﴿وَأَجْلِبْ﴾ shout ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ بِخَيْلِكَ وَرَجِلِكَ﴾ they are those who ride and those who walk in [the path of] sins ﴿وَشَارِكْهُمْ فِي الْأَمْوَالِ﴾ the forbidden ones, such as usury and usurpation ﴿وَالْأَوْلَادِ﴾ from fornication ﴿وَعِدْهُمْ﴾ that there is no resurrection and no recompense ﴿وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ﴾ with that ﴿إِلَّا غُرُورًا﴾ falsehood.

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿إِنَّ عِبَادِي﴾ the believers ﴿لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطَانٌ﴾ domination and power ﴿وَكَفَى بِرَبِّكَ وَكِيلًا﴾ a protector for them against you.

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿رَبُّكُمُ الَّذِي يُزْجِي﴾ makes run ﴿لَكُمُ الْفُلْكَ﴾ the ships ﴿فِي الْبَحْرِ لِتَبْتَغُوا﴾ that you may seek ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ the Exalted's, through trade ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ بِكُمْ رَحِيمًا﴾ in subjecting them to you.

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّكُمُ الضُّرُّ﴾ hardship ﴿فِي الْبَحْرِ﴾ fear of drowning ﴿ضَلَّ﴾ vanishes from you ﴿مَنْ تَدْعُونَ﴾ whom you worship among the gods, so you do not call upon them ﴿إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ﴾ the Exalted; for you call upon Him alone, because you are in a hardship which none but He removes ﴿فَلَمَّا نَجَّاكُمْ﴾ from drowning and brought you ﴿إِلَى الْبَرِّ أَعْرَضْتُمْ﴾ from tawḥīd (affirming Allah's oneness) ﴿وَكَانَ الْإِنْسَانُ كَفُورًا﴾ denying favours.

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿أَفَأَمِنْتُمْ أَنْ يَخْسِفَ بِكُمْ جَانِبَ الْبَرِّ﴾ i.e. the earth, as with Qārūn ﴿أَوْ يُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكُمْ حَاصِبًا﴾ i.e. pelt you with pebbles, as with the people of Lot ﴿ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُوا لَكُمْ وَكِيلًا﴾ a protector from it.

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿أَمْ أَمِنْتُمْ أَنْ يُعِيدَكُمْ فِيهِ﴾ i.e. the sea ﴿تَارَةً﴾ time ﴿أُخْرَى فَيُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكُمْ قَاصِفًا مِنَ الرِّيحِ﴾ i.e. a violent wind that passes over nothing without shattering it, so your ship is broken ﴿فَيُغْرِقَكُمْ بِمَا كَفَرْتُمْ﴾ because of your disbelief ﴿ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُوا لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا بِهِ تَبِيعًا﴾ a helper and pursuer who would demand from Us [redress for] what We did to you.

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ كَرَّمْنَا﴾ We have honoured ﴿بَنِي آدَمَ﴾ with knowledge, speech, balanced form and other things, among them their purity after death ﴿وَحَمَلْنَاهُمْ فِي الْبَرِّ﴾ on beasts ﴿وَالْبَحْرِ﴾ on ships ﴿وَرَزَقْنَاهُمْ مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ وَفَضَّلْنَاهُمْ عَلَى كَثِيرٍ مِمَّنْ خَلَقْنَا﴾ such as cattle and wild beasts ﴿تَفْضِيلًا﴾ So مَنْ here has the meaning of مَا; or it keeps its usual sense and includes the angels, the intended meaning being the preference of the genus, which does not entail the preference of its individuals, since they [the angels] are better than humans other than the prophets. Remember:

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿يَوْمَ نَدْعُوا كُلَّ أُنَاسٍ بِإِمَامِهِمْ﴾ their prophet, so it will be said: "O community of so-and-so"; or by the record of their deeds, so it will be said: "O doer of good, O doer of evil"; and that is the Day of Resurrection ﴿فَمَنْ أُوتِيَ﴾ of them ﴿كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ﴾ they are the fortunate, people of insight in the world ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ يَقْرَءُونَ كِتَابَهُمْ وَلَا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ they will not be shortchanged of their deeds ﴿فَتِيلًا﴾ by the measure of the thread [in the cleft] of a date stone.

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿وَمَنْ كَانَ فِي هَذِهِ﴾ i.e. the world ﴿أَعْمَى﴾ to the truth ﴿فَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ أَعْمَى﴾ to the path of salvation and to reading the Quran ﴿وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا﴾ farther in way from it. And [the following] was revealed concerning Thaqīf, when they had asked him ﷺ to declare their valley sacred and had pressed him insistently.

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ lightened [from إِنَّ] ﴿كَادُوا﴾ they came close ﴿لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ﴾ to bring you down ﴿عَنِ الَّذِي أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ لِتَفْتَرِيَ عَلَيْنَا غَيْرَهُ وَإِذًا﴾ had you done that ﴿لَاتَّخَذُوكَ خَلِيلًا﴾

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿وَلَوْلَا أَنْ ثَبَّتْنَاكَ﴾ upon the truth, through protection [from sin] ﴿لَقَدْ كِدْتَ﴾ you came close ﴿تَرْكَنُ﴾ to inclining ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ شَيْئًا﴾ an inclining ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ because of the intensity of their scheming and insistence. And this is explicit that he ﷺ neither inclined nor came close [to it].

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿إِذًا﴾ had you inclined ﴿لَأَذَقْنَاكَ ضِعْفَ﴾ the punishment of ﴿الْحَيَاةِ وَضِعْفَ﴾ the punishment of ﴿الْمَمَاتِ﴾ i.e. twice what others are punished in this world and the Hereafter ﴿ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُ لَكَ عَلَيْنَا نَصِيرًا﴾ one to prevent it.

celaleyn:76-76.t: And it was revealed when the Jews said to him: "If you are truly a prophet, then go to Syria, for it is the land of the prophets." ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ lightened [from إِنَّ] ﴿كَادُوا لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾ the land of Medina ﴿لِيُخْرِجُوكَ مِنْهَا وَإِذًا﴾ had they expelled you ﴿لَا يَلْبَثُونَ خِلَافَكَ﴾ in it ﴿إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾ then they would be destroyed.

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿سُنَّةَ مَنْ قَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ مِنْ رُسُلِنَا﴾ i.e. like Our way with them, of destroying whoever expelled them ﴿وَلَا تَجِدُ لِسُنَّتِنَا تَحْوِيلًا﴾ change.

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿أَقِمِ الصَّلَوةَ لِدُلُوكِ الشَّمْسِ﴾ i.e. from the time of its declining [from the zenith] ﴿إِلَى غَسَقِ اللَّيْلِ﴾ the onset of darkness, i.e. Ẓuhr, ʿAṣr, Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾ the dawn prayer ﴿إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾ witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day.

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَتَهَجَّدْ﴾ pray ﴿بِهِ﴾ with the Quran ﴿نَافِلَةً لَكَ﴾ an additional obligation for you and not your community; or a merit beyond the obligatory prayers ﴿عَسَى أَنْ يَبْعَثَكَ﴾ will raise you ﴿رَبُّكَ﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿مَقَامًا مَحْمُودًا﴾ in which the first and the last will praise you; it is the station of intercession at the final judgement. And [the following] was revealed when he was commanded to emigrate:

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿وَقُلْ رَبِّ أَدْخِلْنِي﴾ Medina ﴿مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ﴾ an agreeable entry in which I see nothing I dislike ﴿وَأَخْرِجْنِي﴾ from Mecca ﴿مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ﴾ a departure in which my heart does not turn back to it ﴿وَاجْعَلْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ سُلْطَانًا نَصِيرًا﴾ a strength by which You help me against Your enemies.

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿وَقُلْ﴾ upon your entering Mecca: ﴿جَاءَ الْحَقُّ﴾ Islam ﴿وَزَهَقَ الْبَاطِلُ﴾ disbelief has become void ﴿إِنَّ الْبَاطِلَ كَانَ زَهُوقًا﴾ vanishing and passing away. He ﷺ entered it while around the House there were three hundred and sixty idols, and he began striking them with a stick in his hand, saying this, until they fell. Narrated by the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhārī and Muslim].

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ﴾ for explication (li-l-bayān) ﴿الْقُرْآنِ مَا هُوَ شِفَاءٌ﴾ from misguidance ﴿وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ in it ﴿وَلَا يَزِيدُ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the disbelievers ﴿إِلَّا خَسَارًا﴾ because of their disbelief in it.

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿وَإِذَا أَنْعَمْنَا عَلَى الْإِنْسَانِ﴾ the disbeliever ﴿أَعْرَضَ﴾ from gratitude ﴿وَنَأَى بِجَانِبِهِ﴾ he turned his side away, strutting ﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ﴾ poverty and hardship ﴿كَانَ يَئُوسًا﴾ despairing of Allah's mercy.

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿قُلْ كُلٌّ﴾ of us and of you ﴿يَعْمَلُ عَلَى شَاكِلَتِهِ﴾ his way ﴿فَرَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ هُوَ أَهْدَى سَبِيلًا﴾ in way, and He will reward him.

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ﴾ i.e. the Jews ﴿عَنِ الرُّوحِ﴾ by which the body lives ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿الرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّي﴾ i.e. His knowledge; you do not know it ﴿وَمَا أُوتِيتُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾ in relation to His knowledge, the Exalted.

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿وَلَئِنْ﴾ the lām of the oath ﴿شِئْنَا لَنَذْهَبَنَّ بِالَّذِي أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ﴾ i.e. the Quran, by erasing it from the breasts and the copies ﴿ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُ لَكَ بِهِ عَلَيْنَا وَكِيلًا﴾

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ but We have preserved it ﴿رَحْمَةً مِنْ رَبِّكَ إِنَّ فَضْلَهُ كَانَ عَلَيْكَ كَبِيرًا﴾ great, in that He sent it down to you and gave you the Praised Station and other merits.

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿قُلْ لَئِنِ اجْتَمَعَتِ الْإِنْسُ وَالْجِنُّ عَلَى أَنْ يَأْتُوا بِمِثْلِ هَذَا الْقُرْآنِ﴾ in eloquence and rhetorical excellence ﴿لَا يَأْتُونَ بِمِثْلِهِ وَلَوْ كَانَ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ ظَهِيرًا﴾ a helper. It was revealed in rebuttal of their saying: "If we wished, we could say the like of this."

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَا﴾ We have set forth clearly ﴿لِلنَّاسِ فِي هَذَا الْقُرْآنِ مِنْ كُلِّ مَثَلٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted noun, i.e. "a similitude of the kind of every similitude", so that they may take admonition ﴿فَأَبَى أَكْثَرُ النَّاسِ﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca ﴿إِلَّا كُفُورًا﴾ denial of the truth.

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ conjoined to أَبَى ﴿لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّى تَفْجُرَ لَنَا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ يَنْبُوعًا﴾ a spring from which water gushes.

celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿أَوْ تَكُونَ لَكَ جَنَّةٌ﴾ a garden ﴿مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَعِنَبٍ فَتُفَجِّرَ الْأَنْهَارَ خِلَالَهَا﴾ in its midst ﴿تَفْجِيرًا﴾

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿أَوْ تُسْقِطَ السَّمَاءَ كَمَا زَعَمْتَ عَلَيْنَا كِسَفًا﴾ in pieces ﴿أَوْ تَأْتِيَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ قَبِيلًا﴾ face to face and openly, so that we see them.

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿أَوْ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيْتٌ مِنْ زُخْرُفٍ﴾ gold ﴿أَوْ تَرْقَى﴾ you ascend ﴿فِي السَّمَاءِ﴾ on a ladder ﴿وَلَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ﴾ even if you ascended into it ﴿حَتَّى تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْنَا﴾ from it ﴿كِتَابًا﴾ containing confirmation of you ﴿نَقْرَؤُهُ قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿سُبْحَانَ رَبِّي﴾ an expression of astonishment ﴿هَلْ﴾ not (هَلْ = مَا) ﴿كُنْتُ إِلَّا بَشَرًا رَسُولًا﴾ like the rest of the messengers, and they never brought a sign except by Allah's leave.

celaleyn:94-94.t: ﴿وَمَا مَنَعَ النَّاسَ أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا إِذْ جَاءَهُمُ الْهُدَى إِلَّا أَنْ قَالُوا﴾ i.e. their saying, in denial: ﴿أَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ بَشَرًا رَسُولًا﴾ and did not send an angel?

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿لَوْ كَانَ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ instead of humans ﴿مَلَائِكَةٌ يَمْشُونَ مُطْمَئِنِّينَ لَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَلَكًا رَسُولًا﴾ since a messenger is sent to a people only from their own kind, so that they can address him and understand from him.

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿قُلْ كَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ﴾ to my truthfulness ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِ خَبِيرًا بَصِيرًا﴾ knowing their inner and outer states.

celaleyn:97-97.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَهْدِ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ الْمُهْتَدِ وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُمْ أَوْلِيَاءَ﴾ to guide them ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ وَنَحْشُرُهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾ walking ﴿عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ عُمْيًا وَبُكْمًا وَصُمًّا مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ كُلَّمَا خَبَتْ﴾ its flame subsides ﴿زِدْنَاهُمْ سَعِيرًا﴾ flaming and blazing.

celaleyn:98-98.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ جَزَاؤُهُمْ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِنَا وَقَالُوا﴾ denying the resurrection ﴿أَإِذَا كُنَّا عِظَامًا وَرُفَاتًا أَإِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ خَلْقًا جَدِيدًا﴾

celaleyn:99-99.t: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ﴾ know ﴿اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ قَادِرٌ﴾ despite their greatness ﴿عَلَى أَنْ يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُمْ وَجَعَلَ﴾ i.e. the humans, in [their] smallness ﴿لَهُمْ أَجَلًا﴾ for death and resurrection ﴿لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ فَأَبَى الظَّالِمُونَ إِلَّا كُفُورًا﴾ denial of it.

celaleyn:100-100.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿لَوْ أَنْتُمْ تَمْلِكُونَ خَزَائِنَ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّي﴾ of provision and rain ﴿إِذًا لَأَمْسَكْتُمْ﴾ you would be stingy ﴿خَشْيَةَ الْإِنْفَاقِ﴾ fearing their exhaustion through spending, and so be niggardly ﴿وَكَانَ الْإِنْسَانُ قَتُورًا﴾ miserly.

celaleyn:101-101.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى تِسْعَ آيَاتٍ بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ clear: they are the hand, the staff, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the obliteration, the years [of drought] and the shortage of fruits ﴿فَاسْأَلْ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ about it, a question to make the idolaters acknowledge your truthfulness; or [the sense is]: so We said to him: "Ask". In one reading it is in the past-tense form ﴿إِذْ جَاءَهُمْ فَقَالَ لَهُ فِرْعَوْنُ إِنِّي لَأَظُنُّكَ يَا مُوسَى مَسْحُورًا﴾ deceived, overcome in your mind. [Translator's note: the text lists ten items for "nine signs"; translated as written.]

celaleyn:102-102.t: ﴿قَالَ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا أَنْزَلَ هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ signs ﴿إِلَّا رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ بَصَائِرَ﴾ lessons, but you are being obstinate. In one reading [عَلِمْتُ] with ḍamma on the tāʾ ﴿وَإِنِّي لَأَظُنُّكَ يَا فِرْعَوْنُ مَثْبُورًا﴾ destroyed, or turned away from good.

celaleyn:103-103.t: ﴿فَأَرَادَ﴾ Pharaoh ﴿أَنْ يَسْتَفِزَّهُمْ﴾ to expel Moses and his people ﴿مِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾ the land of Egypt ﴿فَأَغْرَقْنَاهُ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ جَمِيعًا﴾

celaleyn:104-104.t: ﴿وَقُلْنَا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ لِبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ اسْكُنُوا الْأَرْضَ فَإِذَا جَاءَ وَعْدُ الْآخِرَةِ﴾ i.e. the Hour ﴿جِئْنَا بِكُمْ لَفِيفًا﴾ all together, you and they.

celaleyn:105-105.t: ﴿وَبِالْحَقِّ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿وَبِالْحَقِّ﴾ which it contains ﴿نَزَلَ﴾ as it was sent down, no alteration having befallen it ﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿إِلَّا مُبَشِّرًا﴾ to whoever believes, of Paradise ﴿وَنَذِيرًا﴾ to whoever disbelieves, of the Fire.

celaleyn:106-106.t: ﴿وَقُرْآنًا﴾ accusative (manṣūb) by a verb which is explained by ﴿فَرَقْنَاهُ﴾ We sent it down in portions over twenty years, or twenty-three ﴿لِتَقْرَأَهُ عَلَى النَّاسِ عَلَى مُكْثٍ﴾ with leisure and deliberateness, so that they understand it ﴿وَنَزَّلْنَاهُ تَنْزِيلًا﴾ one part after another, according to what was beneficial.

celaleyn:107-107.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to the disbelievers of Mecca ﴿آمِنُوا بِهِ أَوْ لَا تُؤْمِنُوا﴾ a threat to them ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾ before its revelation; they are the believers among the People of the Book ﴿إِذَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْهِمْ يَخِرُّونَ لِلْأَذْقَانِ سُجَّدًا﴾

celaleyn:108-108.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّنَا﴾ declaring Him free of breaking a promise ﴿إِنْ﴾ lightened [from إِنَّ] ﴿كَانَ وَعْدُ رَبِّنَا﴾ of its revelation and of the sending of the Prophet ﷺ ﴿لَمَفْعُولًا﴾

celaleyn:109-109.t: ﴿وَيَخِرُّونَ لِلْأَذْقَانِ يَبْكُونَ﴾ a conjunction (ʿaṭf) with an additional description ﴿وَيَزِيدُهُمْ﴾ the Quran ﴿خُشُوعًا﴾ humility before Allah. He ﷺ used to say "O Raḥmān", so they said: "He forbids us to worship two gods while he calls upon another god besides Him." So [the following] was revealed:

celaleyn:110-110.t: ﴿قُلِ﴾ to them ﴿ادْعُوا اللَّهَ أَوِ ادْعُوا الرَّحْمَنَ﴾ i.e. name Him by either of them, or call upon Him by saying "O Allah, O Raḥmān" ﴿أَيًّا﴾ conditional ﴿مَا﴾ redundant (zāʾida), i.e. whichever of these two ﴿تَدْعُوا﴾ it is good; this [apodosis] is indicated by ﴿فَلَهُ﴾ i.e. to the One named by them both ﴿الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى﴾ and these two are among them. For they are, as in the hadith: اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الرَّحْمَنُ الرَّحِيمُ الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلَامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ الْخَالِقُ الْبَارِئُ الْمُصَوِّرُ الْغَفَّارُ الْقَهَّارُ الْوَهَّابُ الرَّزَّاقُ الْفَتَّاحُ الْعَلِيمُ الْقَابِضُ الْبَاسِطُ الْخَافِضُ الرَّافِعُ الْمُعِزُّ الْمُذِلُّ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ الْحَكَمُ الْعَدْلُ اللَّطِيفُ الْخَبِيرُ الْحَلِيمُ الْعَظِيمُ الْغَفُورُ الشَّكُورُ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ الْحَفِيظُ الْمُقِيتُ الْحَسِيبُ الْجَلِيلُ الْكَرِيمُ الرَّقِيبُ الْمُجِيبُ الْوَاسِعُ الْحَكِيمُ الْوَدُودُ الْمَجِيدُ الْبَاعِثُ الشَّهِيدُ الْحَقُّ الْوَكِيلُ الْقَوِيُّ الْمَتِينُ الْوَلِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ الْمُحْصِي الْمُبْدِئُ الْمُعِيدُ الْمُحْيِي الْمُمِيتُ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ الْوَاجِدُ الْمَاجِدُ الْوَاحِدُ الْأَحَدُ الصَّمَدُ الْقَادِرُ الْمُقْتَدِرُ الْمُقَدِّمُ الْمُؤَخِّرُ الْأَوَّلُ الْآخِرُ الظَّاهِرُ الْبَاطِنُ الْوَالِي الْمُتَعَالِ الْبَرُّ التَّوَّابُ الْمُنْتَقِمُ الْعَفُوُّ الرَّؤُوفُ مَالِكُ الْمُلْكِ ذُو الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ الْمُقْسِطُ الْجَامِعُ الْغَنِيُّ الْمُغْنِي الْمَانِعُ الضَّارُّ النَّافِعُ النُّورُ الْهَادِي الْبَدِيعُ الْبَاقِي الْوَارِثُ الرَّشِيدُ الصَّبُورُ [Translator's note: the divine names are kept in Arabic script as listed in the source.] Narrated by al-Tirmidhī. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَا تَجْهَرْ بِصَلَاتِكَ﴾ with your recitation in it, lest the idolaters hear you and revile you, the Quran and the One who sent it down ﴿وَلَا تُخَافِتْ﴾ make it silent ﴿بِهَا﴾ so that your Companions may benefit ﴿وَابْتَغِ﴾ aim for ﴿بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ﴾ between loudness and silence ﴿سَبِيلًا﴾ a middle way.

celaleyn:111-111.t: ﴿وَقُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي لَمْ يَتَّخِذْ وَلَدًا وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ شَرِيكٌ فِي الْمُلْكِ﴾ in divinity ﴿وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وَلِيٌّ﴾ to help Him ﴿مِنَ﴾ on account of ﴿الذُّلِّ﴾ i.e. He is not abased so as to need a helper ﴿وَكَبِّرْهُ تَكْبِيرًا﴾ magnify Him with complete magnification above taking a child, a partner, abasement and everything unbefitting Him. Placing the praise upon that indicates that He is the One deserving of all praises, because of the perfection of His essence and His uniqueness in His attributes. Imam Aḥmad narrated in his Musnad from Muʿādh al-Juhanī from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he used to say: "The verse of might: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي لَمْ يَتَّخِذْ وَلَدًا وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ شَرِيكٌ فِي الْمُلْكِ to the end of the sura." And Allah the Exalted knows best.

celaleyn:1-1.t:
﴿سُبْحَانَ﴾ i.e. transcendence [belongs to] ﴿الَّذِي أَسْرَى بِعَبْدِهِ﴾ Muhammad ﷺ ﴿لَيْلًا﴾ accusative as a ẓarf (adverbial); the isrāʾ is travelling by night, and the benefit of mentioning it is to indicate, by its indefiniteness, the shortness of its duration ﴿مِنَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ﴾ i.e. Mecca ﴿إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَى﴾ Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), [so called] because of its distance from it ﴿الَّذِي بَارَكْنَا حَوْلَهُ﴾ with fruits and rivers ﴿لِنُرِيَهُ مِنْ آيَاتِنَا﴾ the wonders of Our power ﴿إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ﴾ i.e. the One who knows the words and deeds of the Prophet ﷺ; so He favoured him with the Night Journey, which included his meeting the prophets, his ascension to heaven, his seeing the wonders of the dominion (al-malakūt) and his intimate converse with Him, exalted is He. For he ﷺ said:

"I was brought al-Burāq, a white animal larger than a donkey and smaller than a mule, which places its hoof at the furthest reach of its sight. I mounted it and it carried me until I came to Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis). I tied the animal to the ring to which the prophets tie [their mounts], then I entered and prayed two rakʿas in it. Then I came out, and Jibrīl brought me a vessel of wine and a vessel of milk, and I chose the milk. Jibrīl said: 'You have chosen the natural disposition (al-fiṭra).' He said: Then I was taken up to the nearest heaven, and Jibrīl asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Jibrīl.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'And has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and there I was with Adam, who welcomed me and prayed for good for me. Then I was taken up to the second heaven, and Jibrīl asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Jibrīl.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'And has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and there were the two maternal cousins, Yaḥyā and ʿĪsā, who welcomed me and prayed for good for me. Then I was taken up to the third heaven, and Jibrīl asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Jibrīl.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'And has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and there I was with Yūsuf, and he had been given half of all beauty; he welcomed me and prayed for good for me. Then we were taken up to the fourth heaven, and Jibrīl asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Jibrīl.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'And has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and there I was with Idrīs, who welcomed me and prayed for good for me. Then we were taken up to the fifth heaven, and Jibrīl asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Jibrīl.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'And has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and there I was with Hārūn, who welcomed me and prayed for good for me. Then we were taken up to the sixth heaven, and Jibrīl asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Jibrīl.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'And has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and there I was with Mūsā, who welcomed me and prayed for good for me. Then we were taken up to the seventh heaven, and Jibrīl asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Jibrīl.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'And has he been sent for?' He said: 'He has been sent for.' So it was opened for us, and there I was with Ibrāhīm, leaning his back against the Much-Frequented House (al-Bayt al-Maʿmūr), into which seventy thousand angels enter every day and then never return to it. Then he took me to the Lote-Tree of the Boundary (al-Sidra al-Muntahā); its leaves were like the ears of elephants and its fruits like large jars. And when there covered it, of the command of Allah, what covered it, it changed, so that none of Allah the Exalted's creation is able to describe it, for its beauty. He said: Then Allah revealed to me what He revealed, and He made obligatory upon me fifty prayers in every day and night. I descended until I reached Mūsā, who said: 'What has your Lord made obligatory upon your community?' I said: 'Fifty prayers in every day and night.' He said: 'Go back to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction, for your community will not be able to bear that; I have tested the Children of Israel and tried them.' He said: So I went back to my Lord and said: 'O my Lord, lighten [it] for my community,' and He took five off for me. I went back to Mūsā, and he said: 'What did you do?' I said: 'He has taken five off for me.' He said: 'Your community will not be able to bear that, so go back to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction for your community.' He said: So I kept going back and forth between my Lord and Mūsā, and He kept taking off five at a time, until He said: 'O Muhammad, they are five prayers in every day and night, each prayer counting as ten, so that makes fifty prayers. Whoever intends a good deed and does not do it, a good deed is written for him, and if he does it, ten are written for him; and whoever intends an evil deed and does not do it, it is not written, and if he does it, a single evil deed is written for him.' Then I descended until I reached Mūsā and told him, and he said: 'Go back to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction for your community, for your community will not be able to bear that.' I said: 'I have gone back to my Lord until I feel ashamed.'"

Narrated by the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhārī and Muslim], and the wording is Muslim's. And al-Ḥākim narrated in al-Mustadrak from Ibn ʿAbbās: the Messenger of Allah said: "I saw my Lord, Mighty and Majestic is He." The Exalted said:

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَآتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Torah ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهُ هُدًى لِبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ أَلَّا يَتَّخِذُوا مِنْ دُونِي وَكِيلًا﴾ to whom they entrust their affairs; and in one reading [تَتَّخِذُوا] with the upper-dotted letter (tāʾ), as a shift (iltifāt), in which case "an" is redundant (zāʾida) and a verb of saying is implied.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿ذُرِّيَّةَ مَنْ حَمَلْنَا مَعَ نُوحٍ﴾ in the Ark ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَبْدًا شَكُورًا﴾ abundantly thankful to Us, praising [Us] in all his states.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَقَضَيْنَا﴾ We revealed ﴿إِلَى بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Torah ﴿لَتُفْسِدُنَّ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ the land of Syria, through acts of disobedience ﴿مَرَّتَيْنِ وَلَتَعْلُنَّ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا﴾ you will transgress with a great transgression.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿فَإِذَا جَاءَ وَعْدُ أُولَاهُمَا﴾ the first of the two times of corruption ﴿بَعَثْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ عِبَادًا لَنَا أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾ possessed of strength in war and assault ﴿فَجَاسُوا﴾ went to and fro seeking you ﴿خِلَالَ الدِّيَارِ﴾ in the midst of your homes, to kill you and take you captive ﴿وَكَانَ وَعْدًا مَفْعُولًا﴾ They committed the first corruption by killing Zakariyyā, so Jālūt (Goliath) and his troops were sent against them; they killed them, took their children captive and laid waste to Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis).

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَا لَكُمُ الْكَرَّةَ﴾ the turn of power and the upper hand ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ after a hundred years, through the killing of Jālūt ﴿وَأَمْدَدْنَاكُمْ بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ أَكْثَرَ نَفِيرًا﴾ in kinsfolk; and We said:

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿إِنْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ﴾ through obedience ﴿أَحْسَنْتُمْ لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ because its reward is for them ﴿وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ﴾ through corruption ﴿فَلَهَا﴾ is your evil-doing ﴿فَإِذَا جَاءَ وَعْدُ﴾ the time ﴿الْآخِرَةِ﴾ We sent them ﴿لِيَسُوءُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾ to grieve you through killing and captivity, with a grief that shows on your faces ﴿وَلِيَدْخُلُوا الْمَسْجِدَ﴾ Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), and lay it waste ﴿كَمَا دَخَلُوهُ﴾ and laid it waste ﴿أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَلِيُتَبِّرُوا﴾ destroy ﴿مَا عَلَوْا﴾ what they overcame ﴿تَتْبِيرًا﴾ with destruction. They committed corruption a second time by killing Yaḥyā, so He sent against them Bukhtunaṣṣar (Nebuchadnezzar), who killed thousands of them, took their offspring captive and laid waste to Jerusalem.

celaleyn:8-8.t: And We said in the Book: ﴿عَسَى رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ يَرْحَمَكُمْ﴾ after the second time, if you repent ﴿وَإِنْ عُدْتُمْ﴾ to corruption ﴿عُدْنَا﴾ to punishment. And they did return, by denying Muhammad ﷺ, so he was given power over them, with the killing of Qurayẓa, the banishment of Banū al-Naḍīr and the imposition of the jizya upon them ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكَافِرِينَ حَصِيرًا﴾ a place of confinement and a prison.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿إِنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي﴾ i.e. to the way which ﴿هِيَ أَقْوَمُ﴾ most just and most correct ﴿وَيُبَشِّرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ الصَّالِحَاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا كَبِيرًا﴾

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَ﴾ it informs ﴿أَنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ أَعْتَدْنَا﴾ We have prepared ﴿لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ painful; it is the Fire.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَيَدْعُ الْإِنْسَانُ بِالشَّرِّ﴾ against himself and his family when he is vexed ﴿دُعَاءَهُ﴾ i.e. like his praying for himself ﴿بِالْخَيْرِ وَكَانَ الْإِنْسَانُ﴾ the species ﴿عَجُولًا﴾ in praying against himself and not considering its consequence.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ آيَتَيْنِ﴾ indicating Our power ﴿فَمَحَوْنَا آيَةَ اللَّيْلِ﴾ We blotted out its light with darkness so that you may rest in it; the iḍāfa (genitive construct) is explicative ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا آيَةَ النَّهَارِ مُبْصِرَةً﴾ i.e. one in which there is seeing, by the light ﴿لِتَبْتَغُوا﴾ in it ﴿فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ through earning ﴿وَلِتَعْلَمُوا﴾ by both of them ﴿عَدَدَ السِّنِينَ وَالْحِسَابَ﴾ of times ﴿وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾ that is needed ﴿فَصَّلْنَاهُ تَفْصِيلًا﴾ We have explained it clearly.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَكُلَّ إِنْسَانٍ أَلْزَمْنَاهُ طَائِرَهُ﴾ his deeds, which he carries ﴿فِي عُنُقِهِ﴾ it is singled out for mention because attachment there is firmest. Mujāhid said: no child is born but that there is on his neck a leaf on which is written "wretched" or "blessed" ﴿وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ كِتَابًا﴾ in which his deeds are written ﴿يَلْقَاهُ مَنْشُورًا﴾ two adjectives (ṣifa) of كِتَابًا; and it will be said to him:

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿اقْرَأْ كِتَابَكَ كَفَى بِنَفْسِكَ الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكَ حَسِيبًا﴾ a reckoner.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿مَنِ اهْتَدَى فَإِنَّمَا يَهْتَدِي لِنَفْسِهِ﴾ because the reward of his being guided is his ﴿وَمَنْ ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيْهَا﴾ because its sin is upon it ﴿وَلَا تَزِرُ﴾ a soul ﴿وَازِرَةٌ﴾ sinful, i.e. does not bear ﴿وِزْرَ﴾ the burden of a soul ﴿أُخْرَى وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ﴾ anyone ﴿حَتَّى نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًا﴾ who makes clear to him what is obligatory upon him.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَإِذَا أَرَدْنَا أَنْ نُهْلِكَ قَرْيَةً أَمَرْنَا مُتْرَفِيهَا﴾ its affluent ones, in the sense of its chiefs, [We commanded them] to obedience on the tongues of Our messengers ﴿فَفَسَقُوا فِيهَا﴾ and they departed from Our command ﴿فَحَقَّ عَلَيْهَا الْقَوْلُ﴾ of punishment ﴿فَدَمَّرْنَاهَا تَدْمِيرًا﴾ We destroyed it by destroying its people and laying it waste.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿وَكَمْ﴾ i.e. many ﴿أَهْلَكْنَا مِنَ الْقُرُونِ﴾ nations ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ نُوحٍ وَكَفَى بِرَبِّكَ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِ خَبِيرًا بَصِيرًا﴾ knowing their inward and outward aspects; and بِذُنُوبِ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿مَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ﴾ by his deeds ﴿الْعَاجِلَةَ﴾ i.e. this world ﴿عَجَّلْنَا لَهُ فِيهَا مَا نَشَاءُ لِمَنْ نُرِيدُ﴾ to hasten [it] for him; a badal (substitute) for لَهُ, with the preposition repeated ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا لَهُ﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَاهَا﴾ he will enter it ﴿مَذْمُومًا﴾ blamed ﴿مَدْحُورًا﴾ banished from mercy.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَمَنْ أَرَادَ الْآخِرَةَ وَسَعَى لَهَا سَعْيَهَا﴾ did the deeds befitting it ﴿وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ كَانَ سَعْيُهُمْ مَشْكُورًا﴾ with Allah, i.e. accepted and rewarded.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿كُلًّا﴾ of the two groups ﴿نُمِدُّ﴾ We give ﴿هَؤُلَاءِ وَهَؤُلَاءِ﴾ a badal (substitute) ﴿مِنْ﴾ attached (mutaʿalliq) to نُمِدُّ ﴿عَطَاءِ رَبِّكَ﴾ in this world ﴿وَمَا كَانَ عَطَاءُ رَبِّكَ﴾ in it ﴿مَحْظُورًا﴾ withheld from anyone.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿انْظُرْ كَيْفَ فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ﴾ in provision and rank ﴿وَلَلْآخِرَةُ أَكْبَرُ﴾ greater ﴿دَرَجَاتٍ وَأَكْبَرُ تَفْضِيلًا﴾ than this world, so one should attend to it rather than to this world.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿لَا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ فَتَقْعُدَ مَذْمُومًا مَخْذُولًا﴾ with no helper for you.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿وَقَضَى﴾ commanded ﴿رَبُّكَ﴾ ﴿أَنْ﴾ i.e. "bi-an" (that) ﴿لَا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ﴾ that you do good ﴿وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا﴾ by being dutiful to them ﴿إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِنْدَكَ الْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَا﴾ fāʿil (agent) ﴿أَوْ كِلَاهُمَا﴾ and in one reading [يَبْلُغَانِ], in which case أَحَدُهُمَا is a badal (substitute) for its alif ﴿فَلَا تَقُلْ لَهُمَا أُفٍّ﴾ with fatḥa or kasra on the fāʾ, with tanwīn and without it; a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of "perdition!" and "ugliness!" ﴿وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا﴾ scold them ﴿وَقُلْ لَهُمَا قَوْلًا كَرِيمًا﴾ fine and gentle.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿وَاخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ الذُّلِّ﴾ lower your humble side gently to them ﴿مِنَ الرَّحْمَةِ﴾ i.e. out of your tenderness toward them ﴿وَقُلْ رَبِّ ارْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا﴾ they had mercy on me when ﴿رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرًا﴾

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿رَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا فِي نُفُوسِكُمْ﴾ of harbouring dutifulness or undutifulness ﴿إِنْ تَكُونُوا صَالِحِينَ﴾ obedient to Allah ﴿فَإِنَّهُ كَانَ لِلْأَوَّابِينَ﴾ those who constantly return to His obedience ﴿غَفُورًا﴾ for any sudden lapse that issued from them regarding the rights of parents, while they harbour no undutifulness.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿وَآتِ﴾ give ﴿ذَا الْقُرْبَى﴾ kinship ﴿حَقَّهُ﴾ of kindness and maintaining ties ﴿وَالْمِسْكِينَ وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ وَلَا تُبَذِّرْ تَبْذِيرًا﴾ by spending in other than the obedience of Allah.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُبَذِّرِينَ كَانُوا إِخْوَانَ الشَّيَاطِينِ﴾ i.e. following their way ﴿وَكَانَ الشَّيْطَانُ لِرَبِّهِ كَفُورًا﴾ intensely ungrateful for His blessings; and so is his brother, the squanderer.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿وَإِمَّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمْ﴾ i.e. those mentioned, kinsfolk and those after them, and so do not give to them ﴿ابْتِغَاءَ رَحْمَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكَ تَرْجُوهَا﴾ i.e. in seeking provision that you await to come to you, so that you may give to them from it ﴿فَقُلْ لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَيْسُورًا﴾ gentle and easy, by promising them to give when the provision comes.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿وَلَا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلَى عُنُقِكَ﴾ i.e. do not hold it back from spending altogether ﴿وَلَا تَبْسُطْهَا﴾ in spending ﴿كُلَّ الْبَسْطِ فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُومًا﴾ refers back to the first ﴿مَحْسُورًا﴾ cut off, with nothing left to you; refers back to the second.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ﴾ expands it ﴿لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ﴾ restricts it for whom He wills ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِ خَبِيرًا بَصِيرًا﴾ knowing their inward and outward aspects, so He provides for them according to what is good for them.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا أَوْلَادَكُمْ﴾ by burying them alive ﴿خَشْيَةَ﴾ for fear ﴿إِمْلَاقٍ﴾ of poverty ﴿نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُهُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ إِنَّ قَتْلَهُمْ كَانَ خِطْئًا﴾ a sin ﴿كَبِيرًا﴾ great.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا الزِّنَا﴾ more emphatic than "do not commit it" ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ فَاحِشَةً﴾ ugly ﴿وَسَاءَ﴾ evil is ﴿سَبِيلًا﴾ a way, it.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَمَنْ قُتِلَ مَظْلُومًا فَقَدْ جَعَلْنَا لِوَلِيِّهِ﴾ his heir ﴿سُلْطَانًا﴾ authority over the killer ﴿فَلَا يُسْرِفْ﴾ exceed the bounds ﴿فِي الْقَتْلِ﴾ by killing someone other than his killer, or with other than that with which he was killed ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ مَنْصُورًا﴾

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَأَوْفُوا بِالْعَهْدِ﴾ when you make a covenant with Allah or with people ﴿إِنَّ الْعَهْدَ كَانَ مَسْئُولًا﴾ about.
